name: Lactic acid peel

lead: A lactic acid peel is a mild alpha-hydroxy acid peel used for pigmentation such as melasma and dark under-eye skin.
Published work is a handful of small studies comparing it with glycolic and other peels.

paras: Like other AHA peels it loosens and removes outer skin layers in a controlled superficial way.
Light peels commonly cause stinging, redness, irritation and dryness; deeper or stronger peels carry higher complication risk.

lead: A lactic acid peel is a superficial chemical peel using lactic acid, an alpha-hydroxy acid. Alpha hydroxy acids (AHAs) are described by Wikipedia as the mildest peels, used for fine wrinkles, dryness, uneven pigment and acne [1]. Studies have used it at 15% for periorbital melanosis [2][3] and at 92% for epidermal melasma [4].
Evidence is limited to a few comparative studies, mostly in Indian patients, usually comparing lactic acid against glycolic or trichloroacetic acid peels [2][4][3].

paras: A study of 90 patients with constitutional periorbital melanosis compared 20% glycolic peel, 15% lactic peel and topical 20% vitamin C [2]; a later 90-patient study compared a 12% ferulic acid peel against the same glycolic and lactic peels [3]. Another 90-patient study compared 30% glycolic, 92% lactic and 15% trichloroacetic acid peels in epidermal melasma, assessing efficacy, tolerability and quality-of-life improvement [4].

Wikipedia notes that complications rise with peel depth and can include prolonged redness, pigment changes, milia and skin thinning, and that light peels commonly cause stinging, redness, irritation and dryness. [1]
